Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the interactive chat flows look promising. Before we proceed to a pilot, InfoSec needs a clear statement and diagram showing that interactive sessions (web chat + mobile SDK) can be opted out of model improvement and that third-party subprocessors will not train on session contents.

Specifically, we need:
- A short attestation (one paragraph) that data submitted with the no-train flag is excluded from model improvement.
- A dataflow diagram showing what is retained (request/response logs, KV cache, ephemeral session state), where each item lives, retention periods, and who (internal vendors/subprocessors) can access those artifacts.
- Guidance on how to enforce the opt-out in our integration: header(s), SDK param(s), and any routing implications.
- Any evidence or audit entries we can pull from your Console to prove exclusion for a sample session (one-batch request id).

Can you send this over by EOD Tuesday? We have a security review on Wednesday. If you have a short template attestation we can sign as an addendum to the DPA, that would speed things up.

Thanks,
Kirsten Hale
Director, IT Security
Aurora Retail

Hi Kirsten — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (platform) and Marissa (privacy/legal) so we can produce the attestation + diagram. Quick answers up front:

- Yes: we support a per-request opt-out (no_learn=true) that prevents content from being used for model improvement pipelines.
- Enforcement: the flag is honored at the ingestion tier and triggers an exclusion path; we additionally mark and tag related telemetry so it is excluded from downstream training queues.
- Evidence: Console exposes an audit trail (per-request metadata and a "no_learn" annotation) and an exportable CSV for a given time window.

We'll assemble:
1) a one-paragraph attestation you can append to the DPA,
2) a PNG dataflow (who touches what, retention windows),
3) a short integration snippet for web/mobile, and
4) steps to extract a sample audit trail entry.

Target: deliverables attached by EOD Tuesday PST.

Cheers,
Logan

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Interactive sessions: no-train assertion + dataflow mapping request

Kirsten — attaching the diagram and a draft attestation for review. Highlights from the engineering side: 

- Integration enforcement
  * Web SDK: pass sessionMeta.no_learn = true on init; server-side API: set header X-Redwood-No-Learn: true or query param no_learn=true.
  * Once present, request metadata is written to an isolated queue marked "optout". That queue is visible only to infra and compliance roles and is excluded from the training pipeline by ACL.

- Storage/retention
  * Ephemeral KV (in-memory): TTL 12 hours for interactive turn-level caching (never persisted).
  * Short-term request/response logs: retained in an encrypted S3 bucket for 30 days by default; can be reduced per contract. These logs are accessible to a limited set of subprocessors for debugging (listed in the attestation).
  * Long-term audit trail: immutable audit events (no payloads, only metadata + no_learn flag) are stored 7 years for compliance. No payload data is included.

- Subprocessors
  * Current subprocessors with potential access for debugging: FastOps (support tooling), S3 provider (storage), AuditCloud (immutable logs). List included in attestation; we can provide contractual flow-down language.

- Evidence extraction
  * Console -> Audit -> Session Logs -> filter by request id -> export CSV. Attached is a sample export for a redacted session id that shows the no_learn flag and the routing tag.

Let us know if Aurora requires a shorter retention or an escrow-style access model.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Engineers, Runtime

--
Attachments: session-dataflow-diagram.png, no-train-assertion-template.pdf, sample-audit-export.csv

Subject: Re: Interactive sessions: no-train assertion + dataflow mapping request

Hi Kirsten — attaching the signed attestation template (PDF) and the dataflow PNG. I added a short clause you can attach to your DPA that reads: 

"Redwood Inference hereby confirms that any content associated with a correctly-flagged request (no_learn=true, X-Redwood-No-Learn header set, or SDK sessionMeta.no_learn flag) will be excluded from Redwood’s model improvement, retraining, and research pipelines. Exclusion is enforced at ingestion and is traceable via immutable audit events. Redwood’s subprocessors are contractually barred from using such excluded payloads for the purpose of model training."

We have included the current subprocessors and the role-level access list in the attestation. If Aurora needs an alternate retention (e.g., 7 days) we can reflect that in the DPA addendum.

Next steps: 
- If that clause looks good, confirm and we’ll prepare a DPA addendum for signature.
- If you want sample session IDs for a live export during the Wednesday review, we can provide redacted examples in real-time.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a 20-min call if your review team wants to run through the diagram.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
